full_judgment:
7. The defendant-appellant-opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 contested the petition by filing a written objection denying all allegations of the petitioners and conteded inter alia, that the land measuring 17.72 acres appertaining to plot No. 8165 of Mouza Rameshwarpur P.S. Gabtoli, Bogra are the khas land of the Government recorded in Khatian No. 1. The said land which is under the possession of the Government is being used by local people as a beel/pond for catching fishes and using water for irrigation. The further case of the defendants is that the northern side there is a adarshagram on the east-west side of the said adarshagram there are ponds. That during the recent survey the suit land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 D.C. Bogra. That the Govt. allotted 150 metric tons of wheat for an asrayan scheme of Rameshwarpur and as such on 13.2.2000 the Deputy Commissioner, Bogra has directed the Thana Nirbahi Officer to undertake the measure in respect to withdrew the wheat and complete the work within time and as a result 2.94 acres of land has been taken under the asrayan prokalpa. Defendant opposite parties further stated that the plaintiffs are not poor and landless and according to law they are not entitled to get lease of the suit land (being beel). 

 14. It is stated that the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Bogra has taken up the application filed on 27.4.2000 by the defendants-appellants the opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 for hearing the same on 4.5.2000 and after hearing both sides allowed the prayer of the said opposite parties without disposing of the Misc. Appeal filed by the said defendants appellants and as such the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners have been prejudiced. Hence this revisional application under section 115 C.P.C. 

 15. The learned Advocate Mr. Mazibar Rahman appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Additional District Judge allowing the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant appellant-opposite party. No.1-4 and 6 staying the operation of the order of status quo passed on 17.4.2000 by the learned Subordinate Judge has committed irregularity find illegality. According to him the Omitted fact that the petitioners are the bonafide lease-holders by registered lease deeds executed by the defendant opposite party No. 1 after observing all formalities thereof and there is no prove to show that the said registered lease deeds have been cancelled by the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 is absurd. He has further argued that the object of the Government was to rehabilitate the destitute or shelter less or landless is the asrayan prokalpa taken by the Government and the plaintiff-petitioners have got the lease of the khas land of the Government as landless and that the state policy was to rehabiliate the landless people and as such the learned Additional District Judge while disposing the application of opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 did not apply his judicial mind and he was biased. Learned Advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge acted illegally in holding that the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 are in possession of the suit land and that the learned Subordinate Judge was justified by granting status quo in respect of the suit land but the learned Additional District Judge acted illegally in total misconception and as such the judgment and order is liable to set aside. 

 21. Considering the balance of convenience and inconvenience we find that if any order of injunction at this stage is granted in favour of the petitioners this will surely hinder the development works of the Government and the development scheme which is going financed by the donor agencies will go in vain. After the publication of the E.B. State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 all of these beels/ponds (Jalmahals) of the ex-zaminders vested to the Government free from all incumbrances and permanent lease of these beel lands is prohibited. However, all these points are required to be decided in the main suit after taking proper evidence.
